# Test the arithmetic, then explain the identity

All 30 lessons teach **numerical relationships first**. Use the small [Python file](numerical_math_lab.py) only to verify examples, rather than memorising code as the solution.

From the repository root:

~~~bash
python3 interviews/tips-and-notes/numerical-math/examples/numerical_math_lab.py
python3 -m unittest discover -s interviews/tips-and-notes/numerical-math/examples -p 'test_*.py'
~~~

This standard-library lab checks factorisation identities for multiple positive and negative values, common sums, number-theory relations, bound examples, bit tricks and arithmetic used in the lessons.

A hundred passing numerical tests still would not prove an identity for all inputs. **The algebraic derivations in each chapter are the proofs.**
